solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Contribute 100? Doubly cool!

blocks.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
two words for cool, one after the other: hip and in

explanation.surface: Someone pays a hundred towards a whip-round and is congratulated on being twice as cool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doubly' asks for two different slang words meaning fashionable, set side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: To chip in is an informal phrasal verb for adding your share of money or effort to a common pot.

clue.text: Plum to throw at the bottom of copper

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed at the bottom of another comes after it in the column

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to shy is to fling or toss, as at a coconut shy

explanation.surface: An instruction to lob a plum at the base of a copper pan, or at a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Plum looks like the fruit you might throw, but here it is the adjective in 'a plum job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A plum job and a cushy job are both easy, comfortable, desirable positions requiring little effort.

clue.text: Canine, say, is barking regardless

indicators.note: barking is British slang for mad, so the letters go crazy and rearrange

blocks.note: the letters of both words are the material to rearrange

explanation.surface: A dog, for instance, keeps on barking whatever happens.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking reads as what a canine does, but in Britain it also means mad, which is its job here.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means whatever happens or anyway, used to dismiss other considerations, so it matches regardless as an adverb.

clue.text: State the words of a coward?

blocks.note: a coward confesses to fleeing in two words: the first-person pronoun and the past tense of run

explanation.surface: A demand to report what a coward says.
explanation.walkthrough: State looks like a verb meaning say, but it is the noun: a country. The coward's confession is the two words I and RAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The Middle Eastern country is a sovereign nation, which is a crossword-standard sense of the word state.

clue.text: Chilling mostly after injury — that’s good to hear

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter of that phrase is dropped
after places the chilling part later in the sequence than the injury part

blocks.note: harm is damage or injury
a drink that is chilling is on ice; mostly drops its final E

explanation.surface: Someone relaxing after getting hurt, and a friend replying that it is pleasing news.
explanation.walkthrough: Chilling here is not relaxing but kept cold, on ice. 'That's good to hear' sounds like a reply to news.
explanation.definitionFit: Harmonic describes sounds in harmony, pleasant and musical, so something harmonic is pleasing to the ear.

clue.text: All hooch nearly drunk? Here’s more!

definitions.text: All hooch nearly drunk? Here’s more!

indicators.note: nearly means not quite complete, so the final letter of the phrase is cut
drunk suggests staggering and disorder, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: both words taken as written, minus the last H

explanation.surface: Someone has nearly finished the moonshine, and a host cheerfully produces another bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: when the hooch is almost gone, the drink being offered is more of the same stuff.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooch is cheap liquor, so a fresh supply when the bottle runs dry is more intoxicating spirit.

clue.text: Parent and child clipped plane? Rubbish

indicators.note: something clipped has had its end trimmed off, so the final letter goes

blocks.note: Mum is the British word for mother
a child is a boy; clipped loses its last letter
a jumbo is a jumbo jet, a large aircraft

explanation.surface: A mother and child have a toy plane trimmed, and someone dismisses it as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Mumbo jumbo is meaningless or nonsensical talk, which is one sense of rubbish as a noun.

clue.text: Hear no sound from stable

indicators.note: hear tells us to take the next word as it is spoken, not as it is spelt

blocks.note: nay is an old word for no

explanation.surface: A complaint that no sound at all is coming from the horses' stable.
explanation.definitionFit: A neigh is the high whinnying cry of a horse, the animal kept in a stable.

clue.text: Is a father able to briefly vote for national celebration?

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter of that word is removed

blocks.note: the question 'Is a father able to' can be put as 'Can a dad'
a vote for is an aye; briefly drops the E

explanation.surface: A question whether a dad is allowed to vote for a national holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: Rewrite the opening question in its shorter form and the letters run straight into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Canada Day, on the first of July, is the country's annual holiday marking confederation in 1867.

clue.text: Iron bar sent north over area that covers Indiana?

indicators.note: in a down entry, sending a word north makes it read from bottom to top
in a down entry, a piece over another sits above it, so comes first in the column

blocks.note: Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
a rod is a bar; sent north it reads backwards
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A geography-style puzzle about a metal bar being shipped across a region spanning an American state.
explanation.walkthrough: Indiana is not the US state but Indiana Jones, whose trademark hat is the answer; the question mark flags the trick.
explanation.definitionFit: A fedora is a soft felt brimmed hat, famously worn by the film adventurer Indiana Jones on his head.

clue.text: Confirm a north-eastern shipping route

blocks.note: to seal a deal is to confirm it
taken as written
NE is the compass abbreviation for north-east

explanation.surface: Verifying that a route ships goods along the north-east coast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sea lane is an established course regularly followed by ships crossing open water, so it is a shipping route.

clue.text: Victor ignores second flower

indicators.note: ignoring the second letter means leaving out whatever stands in position two of that word

blocks.note: a victor is a winner, a champion; its second letter H is dropped

explanation.surface: A winning competitor snubs the runner-up at a flower show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Second' looks like the runner-up being ignored, but it means the second letter of the winner's word.
explanation.definitionFit: Campions are wild plants of the pink family with bright pink, red or white blooms, so one is a flower.

clue.text: Be inconsistent, with indignant cry interrupting informal greeting

indicators.note: something interrupting breaks into the middle of another thing, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: yo is a slangy hello
oy is a cry of protest to get attention

explanation.surface: Someone flip-flops, shouting in protest in the middle of saying a casual hello.
explanation.walkthrough: The cry goes between the two letters of the greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To yo-yo is to swing repeatedly up and down or between positions, as the toy on a string does.

clue.text: Scorned AA invention twice by the road, ultimately

indicators.note: twice asks for the same piece to be written two times in a row
ultimately points to the final letter of each word it governs

blocks.note: A. A. Milne created the bear Winnie-the-Pooh
the same creation again
last letter of the
last letter of road

explanation.surface: A motoring organisation's gadget is dismissed out of hand at the roadside.
explanation.walkthrough: AA looks like the Automobile Association, the British breakdown service, which suits the road; it is really the initials of A. A. Milne.
explanation.definitionFit: To pooh-pooh something is to dismiss it as foolish or unimportant, so pooh-poohed means treated with contempt.

clue.text: I have the same women’s clothing on, and a flower?

blocks.note: the cry in the card game when two matching cards appear
drag is women's clothes worn by a man
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone notices they are wearing the identical dress to another guest, and wonders about a flower.
explanation.walkthrough: Snap is the children's card game where you shout the word on spotting a matching pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The snapdragon, or antirrhinum, is a garden plant whose blooms open like a mouth when squeezed, so it is a flower.

clue.text: Screen finally put between hot drink and letters for protection

indicators.note: finally asks for the last letter of the word before it
put between places that letter in the gap between the two neighbouring pieces

blocks.note: chai is spiced tea
last letter of screen
letters are post, mail

explanation.surface: Instructions for shielding your cup of tea from the morning post.
explanation.definitionFit: Chain mail is armour of interlinked metal rings, worn by medieval soldiers as protection in battle.

clue.text: Internet whiz nearby cut off

indicators.note: off means gone bad or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A computer expert living close by finds their connection has been cut off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut off' reads as one phrase, but cut is anagram material and off is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A cybernaut is someone who explores the online world expertly, so an internet whiz in informal terms.

clue.text: Hiked and had something to eat, skipping starter

indicators.note: skipping the starter means passing over the opening letter

blocks.note: supped means took supper; its first letter S goes

explanation.surface: A walker went for a hike and then ate, but skipped the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiked suggests walking in the hills, but here it means raised, as prices are hiked; starter is a pun on the meal's first course.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean increased or raised, as when a company hikes or ups its prices.

clue.text: Official opinion of the conga, perhaps?

blocks.note: first meaning: the policy a political organisation expects members to follow
second meaning, playful: the dancers in a conga form a queue at a celebration

explanation.surface: Asking what the authorities officially think of the conga dance.
explanation.walkthrough: The conga is a dance where people hold the waist of the one in front, forming a long line at a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A party line is the policy stance a political group requires its members to support, an official opinion.

clue.text: Initially, banana skin repelled censor

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of the next word
repelled means driven back, so the word is read backwards

blocks.note: first letter of banana
peel is the skin of fruit; repelled turns it round

explanation.surface: A banana skin slip-up being kept out, like a censored joke.
explanation.definitionFit: To bleep is to cover offensive words in a broadcast with a high tone, which is one way to censor them.

clue.text: Fruit from gloomy northern town you might gather

indicators.note: to gather is to learn by hearsay, so the town is taken as you would hear it

blocks.note: feeling blue is feeling low
Bury is a town near Manchester in north-west England

explanation.surface: Fruit picked from a grey northern town, to be gathered like a harvest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gather' looks like picking fruit, but it means learning by hearsay, so the town is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: The blueberry is a small sweet dark-blue berry grown on shrubs, so it is a type of fruit.

clue.text: Small creature in wine drunk by queen, possibly

indicators.note: something drunk by another goes inside it, swallowed whole

blocks.note: a queen bee is one kind of bee
Asti is an Italian sparkling wine

explanation.surface: A tiny creature found floating in wine that a queen may have drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen points to the royal family, but 'possibly' marks it as an example: a queen is a bee.
explanation.definitionFit: Beastie is a Scottish and playful word for a little animal or insect, as in Burns's poem to a mouse.

clue.text: Worried about small vessels

indicators.note: worried means shaken or tugged at, so the letters are disturbed into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: Someone fretting over little boats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Worried about' looks like a single phrase, but about is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: U-boats were German submarines of the two world wars, and submarines are seagoing vessels.

clue.text: I understand that you may bring home this philosopher

blocks.note: roger is radio talk for message received and understood
to bring home the bacon is an idiom for earning a living

explanation.surface: A dialogue: one person agrees that the other may bring a philosopher home.
explanation.definitionFit: Roger Bacon was a thirteenth-century English friar and thinker who championed experiment, so he is a philosopher.

clue.text: Become large and emit a threatening noise

blocks.note: to grow can mean to become, as in grow old
L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A beast swells to full size and lets out a menacing sound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Become large' reads as one idea, growing big, but the two words give separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog growls by making a low rumbling sound in its throat as a warning, which is a threatening noise.

clue.text: Instrument seen during family reunion

indicators.note: seen during means found within the run of letters that follows

blocks.note: the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: A musical instrument spotted at a family get-together.
explanation.definitionFit: The lyre is an ancient stringed harp-like device played by plucking, so it is a musical instrument.

clue.text: Greet cuckoo and another bird

indicators.note: cuckoo is slang for crazy, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Say hello to a cuckoo and then to a second bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cuckoo' sets up a list of birds, and 'another' plays along; but the cuckoo is only the signal for madness.
explanation.definitionFit: The egret is a white heron with long legs, and it is a different bird from the cuckoo the surface mentions.

clue.text: Muscle problem hit hard when standing up

indicators.note: in a down entry, standing up means reading from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: to tonk is British slang for striking forcefully, as a batsman does

explanation.surface: A sports injury: a muscle seizes up when you are struck hard while upright.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot is a tight painful lump in a muscle, a common source of aches and stiffness.

clue.text: In the middle of a very entertaining new song’s finale

indicators.note: to entertain is to host guests, so this word takes others inside it
a finale is the end, so only the last letter is used

blocks.note: taken as written
most can mean very, as in most kind
N is the abbreviation for new
last letter of song

explanation.surface: Halfway through a show, a highly enjoyable fresh song brings the house down at its close.
explanation.walkthrough: A comes first; the new letter and the song's last letter sit inside the word for very.
explanation.definitionFit: Amongst means surrounded by or among, as in a house amongst trees, so it means in the middle of.

clue.text: Maybe hotter place in Africa

blocks.note: first meaning: sharper in flavour, more tangy, which spicier food may be
second meaning: a port city in Morocco

explanation.surface: A North African location that may have a warmer climate.
explanation.walkthrough: Hotter suggests weather in Africa, but it means spicier; 'maybe' signals that the sense is only loosely related.
explanation.definitionFit: Tangier is a Moroccan port on the Strait of Gibraltar, and the comparative of tangy describes a sharper, spicier taste.

clue.text: Gifted man secures a fast time

indicators.note: to secure is to hold fast, so this piece wraps around the next

blocks.note: Ted is a common man's name
taken as written
Lent is the Christian period of fasting before Easter

explanation.surface: A capable person locks in a quick finishing time in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fast time' reads as a quick race time, but fast is fasting, the Lenten sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone with natural ability or a special aptitude for something.

clue.text: A trial to net billions, if everything goes perfectly

indicators.note: to net is to catch in a net, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: a trial is a test
B is the abbreviation for billions

explanation.surface: An experiment designed to catch billions, if all goes to plan.
explanation.walkthrough: B goes inside the word for trial, after the T.
explanation.definitionFit: At best is an idiom for the most favourable outcome possible, meaning even in the ideal case.
